enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
352 AM MST Tue Nov 3 2026

...New AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 352 AM MST Tue Nov 3 2026

 - Dry weather through Friday with a slight chance of showers
   Friday night and Saturday. 

 - Breezy Wednesday afternoon, otherwise winds on the light side. 

 - Temperatures will run near to slightly below normal through the
   upcoming week.  

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 827 PM MST Mon Nov 2 2026

Winds will decrease through the evening as the upper-level low
moves into the Central-Southern Plains. Some fog may be present in
the southern Gila National Forest in Grant County this morning 
due to recent rains, but lower dew points will be moving into our 
area on Tuesday, keeping conditions mainly dry. Temperatures for 
Tuesday will be 6 to 8 degrees below normal for early November
(mid 60s in the lowlands). The NBM had El Paso be about 5 degrees
cooler than what the MOS guidance for both Tuesday and Wednesday
due to increasing pressure highs aloft allowing for faster diurnal
heating from the sun, despite light cold air advection from the 
north.

Temperatures for Wednesday will be relatively similar to Tuesday,
if not slightly warmer. Winds will increase slightly from the 
west to about 10-15 mph. An upper-level low moving across the
Central Rockies will bring a Pacific cold front through the area
Wednesday afternoon, which will cool temperatures down slightly 
for Thursday. Both models have the low too far north for 
precipitation to affect the region. For the rest of the week, 
conditions will be relatively dry and quiet until Friday, where
the Borderland could see a possible chance of rain--confidence is
low at this time, and the ECMWF is leaning on the wetter side of
things. I am skeptical if we will get any rain at the end of the 
week.

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS) Issued at 352 AM MST Tue Nov 3 2026

VFR conditions through the period with FEW100 SCT-BKN250. Surface
winds variable AOB 7 knots becoming south/southwest 7-10 knots
this afternoon. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 352 AM MST Tue Nov 3 2026

We start a stretch of dry weather today as dry west flow aloft
dominates much of the week. An upper low crossing Colorado 
Wednesday will bring some breezy afternoon winds (west 10-20 mph),
otherwise no significant winds are expected through this weekend.
The next shot at some rain will be Friday night and Saturday as a
Pacific system moves through the area. 

Min RH: Lowlands 30-40% today and Wednesday, decreasing to 25-35%
Thursday through Saturday. Mountains 35-50% through Saturday. 
Vent rates poor-fair through Saturday. 

&&
